questions.question: Which of the following is a common indicator that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: A change in the container's volume
A change in colour, bubbling, or a change of temperature
The complete evaporation of a liquid
A change in the shape of the container

questions.question: Why do bubbles typically appear during a chemical reaction?
options: Because a solid is dissolving into a liquid
Because a gas is being produced
Because the liquid is boiling due to external heat
Because the substances are turning into a plasma

questions.question: What occurs to the atoms of reactants during a chemical reaction?
options: They are destroyed and brand new atoms are created
They rearrange themselves to form new substances
They change into different chemical elements
They melt into a single large nucleus

questions.question: Generally, what is a key characteristic of chemical reactions regarding their reversibility?
options: They can easily be reversed by cooling them down
They are irreversible
They always produce liquid water
They only occur at room temperature

questions.question: Which three components are required to start a combustion reaction?
options: Fuel, carbon dioxide, and a cooling agent
Fuel, oxygen, and an initial source of energy, usually heat
Water, carbon dioxide, and light
Nitrogen, oxygen, and electricity

questions.question: What process does the term 'burning' describe in chemistry?
options: The reaction of substances with oxygen, commonly referring to visible flames
The physical melting of a solid into a liquid
The breaking down of water into hydrogen and oxygen gases
The cooling of a substance until it solidifies

questions.question: Which gas is often formed in a chemical reaction when both oxygen and carbon atoms are present?
options: Nitrogen dioxide
Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen gas
Sulfur dioxide

questions.question: What occurs during a decomposition reaction?
options: Two elements combining to make a single compound
A single compound breaking down into two or more products
An insoluble solid forming from two solutions
A substance reacting rapidly with oxygen to produce heat

questions.question: What do metal carbonates typically form when they decompose upon heating?
options: Metal oxides and carbon dioxide gas
Metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas
Pure metals and oxygen gas
Metal chlorides and water vapour

questions.question: What is the chemical term for a reaction where a substance combines with oxygen?
options: Reduction
Decomposition
Oxidation
Precipitation

questions.question: Which of the following are common examples of oxidation reactions?
options: Melting and freezing
Combustion and rusting
Evaporation and condensation
Filtering and dissolving

questions.question: What happens when a precipitation reaction occurs?
options: A solid melts into a liquid when heated
Two solutions combine to form an insoluble solid
A gas condenses to form a liquid
A single compound breaks down into simpler gases

questions.question: Why are precipitation reactions important in the process of water treatment?
options: To boil the water and kill all bacteria
To remove unwanted substances from water
To increase the oxygen level of drinking water
To convert salt water into fresh water through evaporation

questions.question: According to the conservation of mass, how does the mass of the products compare to the mass of the reactants?
options: The mass of the products is always greater
The mass of the products is the same as the mass of the reactants
The mass of the products is always less
The mass can increase or decrease depending on the temperature

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using word equations in chemistry?
options: To calculate the exact mass of the atoms involved
They are a simple way of describing chemical reactions
To list the physical state of every chemical
To show the speed of a reaction

questions.question: In a chemical equation, what does the arrow represent?
options: The speed of the reaction
The words 'changes into'
The temperature at which the reaction occurs
The physical state of the products
